The year 2026 was already on track to be one of the hottest years on record, continuing the trend of global warming. The heatwaves were caused by a high-pressure system that settled over the continent, causing temperatures to soar.


== Events ==


=== First heatwave ===

The first heatwave began in late June 2026 and affected many countries in western and central Europe, mainly France, Spain, Portugal, Germany and Italy. Temperature records were broken in several countries. France recorded its highest ever temperature of 47.9 °C (118.2 °F) in Toulouse. Spain recorded a temperature of 48.3°C in Seville, surpassing the previous record. Portugal recorded a temperature of 48.0°C in the Alentejo region. Germany recorded a temperature of 42.1°C in the Rhineland, surpassing the previous record of 41.2°C set during 2019.


=== Second heatwave ===

The second heatwave began in mid-July 2026 and mainly affected eastern and southern Europe, mainly Greece, Italy, the Balkans and Turkey, with temperatures regularly reaching over 50 °C in Greece and Turkey. Italy set a new record of 52.1°C in Sicily, and in Greece, a temperature of 50.3°C was recorded on the mainland, while temperatures climbed up to 53.8°C on the island of Crete.
